Operating Characteristics for Quantitative Decisions Comparing Rates

Source: R/f_design_plan_qtd_rates.R
getOperatingCharacteristicsRates.Rd

Calculates probabilities of all six quantitative decision categories by exact summation over two independent binomial event counts.

Usage

getOperatingCharacteristicsRates(
  design,
  ...,
  numberOfSubjects,
  pi1,
  pi2,
  directionUpper = TRUE,
  intervalMethod = "qtd1"
)

Arguments

design

A decision rule from getDesignQuantitative(). Reference values refer to the risk difference in the beneficial direction.

...

Additional arguments are checked for unknown names.

numberOfSubjects

Numeric matrix with two columns, control followed by treatment, and at least one row. Each row is a sample-size scenario; all entries must be positive integers.

pi1

Numeric vector of true treatment event probabilities in [0, 1].

pi2

Single true control event probability in [0, 1].

directionUpper

Whether increasing treatment event rates are beneficial. If TRUE (default), the effect is pi1 - pi2; if FALSE, it is pi2 - pi1.

intervalMethod

One of "qtd1" (default), "farringtonManning", "miettinenNurminen", or "newcombe", as described in plot.TrialDesignPlanQuantitative().

Value

An OperatingCharcteristicsRates object supporting console and Markdown printing, summaries and the QTD plot families. Its probabilities data frame contains category, probability, nControl, nTreatment, alternative, pi1, and pi2. alternative is the true risk difference in the beneficial direction.

Details

Decision boundaries use the same interval calculations and equality rules as the binary decision map. The QTD1 method reproduces the original program, including Wilson limits rounded to four decimal places in its variance construction, and requires lowerPercentile <= 0.5 <= upperPercentile. The other methods support ordered percentiles anywhere in (0, 1). Exact summation describes the sampling distribution of the counts; the interval methods themselves are approximate frequentist constructions.

The six exclusive categories are Go (Fixed), Go, Indeterminate 1, Indeterminate 2, Stop, and Stop (Fixed). Add the two Go, Indeterminate, or Stop categories for the respective three-category probabilities. Each scenario contains six blocks, with the supplied treatment rates in order within each block. Repeated rates and sample-size scenarios are retained. A count grid may contain at most one million cells per sample-size scenario. Counts and probabilities are computed without requiring ggplot2 or Java.

See also

getDesignQuantitative(), getOperatingCharacteristicsMeans(), OperatingCharcteristicsRates, summaryQuantitative, plot.OperatingCharcteristics()

Examples

# Binary example from the original QTD1 demonstration:
rule <- getDesignQuantitative(targetValue = 0, lowerReferenceValue = -0.05)
oc <- getOperatingCharacteristicsRates(rule,
    numberOfSubjects = matrix(c(75, 75, 75, 150), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE),
    pi1 = c(0.1, 0.15, 0.175, 0.2, 0.25), pi2 = 0.15,
    directionUpper = FALSE)
print(oc)
